title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
An Israeli-funded operation created a fake think tank and used it to publish over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days, all designed to influence how AI chatbots respond to queries about Israel. The operation deployed academic-formatted arguments on disputed topics including alleged war crimes, genocide accusations, and starvation, and registered the material with the U.S. Justice Department as foreign propaganda. This shows a failure in the data supply chain to AI systems: material can be generated, formatted as authoritative research, and injected into the information ecosystem that trains commercial chatbots without verification of its source or authenticity.

The system succeeded because nothing in the deployment process caught that the institute had no legal entity, no physical address, and published an implausible volume of material in an implausible timeframe. It would have required either human review of training data sources for basic credibility checks, or detection systems that flag suspicious patterns in bulk publication campaigns, or both. The operation demonstrates that actors with resources can manufacture false institutional authority at scale and that AI systems are not yet built to resist such manipulation in their training phase.

It is not established whether the operation measurably changed chatbot outputs, or how much of the material actually entered commercial training datasets versus circulating as candidate material.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

An Israeli-funded fake think tank called the Hanover Institute published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days using a platform designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots. The nonexistent institute, which has no legal entity status or physical address, presented pro-Israel arguments on contentious topics including alleged war crimes, genocide accusations, and starvation in Gaza in an academic format. The operation was registered with the U.S. Justice Department as Israeli government propaganda material distributed through various intermediaries.

The campaign is part of a broader Israeli government effort financed by tens of millions of dollars routed through European advertising firm Havas Media to manipulate how chatbots respond to queries about Israel. Israeli officials have expressed doubts about the campaign's effectiveness, with some calling it wasteful, while U.S. public opinion has shifted sharply against Israel, with polling showing record low support among Americans. Researchers warn this represents a new threat of artificial intelligence manipulation by foreign governments and other actors seeking to influence training data that feeds commercial AI systems.
